title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
abstract: arXiv:2611.32029v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Occupancy world models predict future 3D scenes conditioned on ego actions, yet their predictions may not faithfully follow the specified trajectory under counterfactual actions. Because driving datasets provide sparse coverage of alternative trajectories for each scene, existing models learn the spatial effect of ego motion implicitly from observed scene--trajectory combinations, which may entangle action effects with scene--trajectory correlations. We propose ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames. ReCast decouples historical encoding from future decoding and aligns deformable interactions using relative ego transformations, while retaining flexibility for non-rigid scene evolution. We also introduce a counterfactual action-faithfulness benchmark covering in-distribution, tail, and out-of-distribution trajectories. On Occ3D-nuSce

translated_title: 占据世界模型真的遵循动作吗？
translated_abstract: 占据世界模型以自车动作为条件预测未来3D场景，然而在反事实动作下，其预测可能无法忠实地遵循指定的轨迹。由于驾驶数据集对每个场景的替代轨迹覆盖稀疏，现有模型只能从观测到的场景-轨迹组合中隐式学习自车运动的空间效应，这可能将动作效应与场景-轨迹相关性纠缠在一起。我们提出ReCast，一种由自车轨迹引导的Transformer，它将未来预测建立在自车中心帧之间由动作引起的几何对应关系之上。ReCast将历史编码与未来解码解耦，并利用相对自车变换对可变形交互进行对齐，同时保持对非刚性场景演化的灵活性。我们还引入了一个反事实动作忠实性基准，涵盖分布内、尾部和分布外轨迹。在Occ3D-nuSce（原文截断）
tldr: 论文提出ReCast模型，通过将未来预测建立在动作引起的自车帧间几何对应关系上，解决了占据世界模型在反事实动作下预测不忠实遵循指定轨迹的问题，并首次引入了反事实动作忠实性评估基准。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames to ensure occupancy world models faithfully follow counterfactual actions, and introduces a counterfactual action-faithfulness benchmark.
